scope: React/Tauri scientific GUI: Calibration, Mask, Integration, Map, Batch, settings and sampled dialogs/editors. Scores assess design, not scientific accuracy or production readiness.
method: 25 independent categories, equal weight of 4% each. Both reviewers use these definitions and anchors. Decimal scores are allowed. No requirement to award a particular score.

scale.1-3: Routine work is blocked or unreliable.
scale.4-6: Usable, but recurring material friction or inconsistency remains.
scale.7-8: Strong design with identifiable gaps in the reviewed workflows.
scale.9-9.5: Polished in the reviewed workflows: key expectations met, no material defect observed in that category, only minor limitations or optional enhancements.
scale.10: Exceptional design supported by broad empirical validation beyond this review.

limits: This is a scoped scientific GUI design assessment, not scientific accuracy, production readiness, or formal accessibility certification. Missing evidence is identified explicitly; intentional documented user choices are not defects.

criteria.name: Scientific context and provenance
criteria.definition: Distinguish fitted, loaded, manual and derived results, their sources and diagnostic limits.

criteria.name: Numeric precision and units
criteria.definition: Keep exact stored values, legible signed display values and explicit scientific units/conventions.

criteria.name: Data visualization clarity
criteria.definition: Make scientific scales, references, labels and color ranges interpretable without suggesting false data.

criteria.name: Plot interaction and inspection
criteria.definition: Preserve original detector resolution, square pixels, shared gestures and linked coordinates.

criteria.name: Workflow usability
criteria.definition: Support common analysis tasks directly and preserve meaningful work during navigation.

criteria.name: Navigation and information architecture
criteria.definition: Use predictable mode/task grouping, persistent actions and clear navigation state.

criteria.name: Discoverability and learnability
criteria.definition: Expose tools, gestures and explanations so users can learn without memorizing hidden actions.

criteria.name: Cognitive load and progressive disclosure
criteria.definition: Keep relevant controls visible while keeping advanced or uncommon operations manageable.

criteria.name: Typography
criteria.definition: Use consistent type sizes, weights, hierarchy, numerals and scientific notation.

criteria.name: Readability and contrast
criteria.definition: Keep labels and values readable, preserve signs, and clearly distinguish inactive controls.

criteria.name: Spacing and alignment
criteria.definition: Maintain deliberate spacing, aligned labels/values, usable tables and stable action placement.

criteria.name: Visual hierarchy
criteria.definition: Let scientific data dominate while keeping state, source context and actions easy to scan.

criteria.name: Visual consistency across modes
criteria.definition: Use the same visual rules for equivalent controls, tabs, dialogs and states.

criteria.name: Component reuse and control semantics
criteria.definition: Give common interface behavior one owner without losing scientific mode responsibilities.

criteria.name: Dialogs and focus management
criteria.definition: Make opening, dismissal, cancellation and focus return predictable, including nested dialogs.

criteria.name: Keyboard efficiency and shortcut accuracy
criteria.definition: Make documented shortcuts operate correctly in the appropriate context without unsafe conflicts.

criteria.name: Accessibility and inclusive use
criteria.definition: Provide names/descriptions, semantic controls, focus visibility, text scaling and recoverable feedback.

criteria.name: System status and feedback
criteria.definition: Show processing, pending changes, stale plots and operation outcomes accurately.

criteria.name: Validation and error prevention
criteria.definition: Prevent incomplete or invalid edits from changing scientific state or misleading users.

criteria.name: Error recovery
criteria.definition: Explain failures without losing scientific work and provide a clear way to continue.

criteria.name: Undo, redo and reversibility
criteria.definition: Make the actual next history operation clear and preserve unrelated scientific diagnostics.

criteria.name: Responsive layout and text scaling
criteria.definition: Keep controls and plots usable at supported compact sizes and both text sizes.

criteria.name: Performance and perceived responsiveness
criteria.definition: Keep navigation and feedback responsive during scientific processing and display updates.

criteria.name: Settings and file workflow reliability
criteria.definition: Preserve deliberate drafts/preferences and make input/output sources and scope clear.

criteria.name: Maintainability and ownership
criteria.definition: Centralize reusable UI policy and keep behavior reviewable and testable.

designConstraints: Mode navigation stays left and task controls right, with neutral charcoal and orange accents.
Maximize scientific data area: compact legends float inside plots and may be moved; never allocate an extra legend header above the data.
Resting text fields use quiet recessed fills without pale outlines. Clear keyboard focus and error states remain visible.
Keep WebGL2 as the normal pattern renderer and preserve exact source values, original detector pixels, shared gestures and local Python processing.
